# Independent audit: ten-point diamond and exact coarse/fine gap

Audited in full:
`candidate a2bca99efffd5fb9` and
`supporting computation verify_ten_point_diamond_filter_depth_gap.py`.


passes, including its invocation of the earlier integer-hull verifier.
No repairs are needed. The coarse-depth lower bound has the explicit
paired-centroid-tail dependency stated in the source; the fine-depth
calculation does not use that theorem.

## 1. Exact support and Helly numbers

The old eleven-point polytope contains conv(W), so it bounds all
possible integer points of the smaller hull. The outlier p_9 is
excluded by y+z, whereas p_2 belongs to either displayed midpoint
pair. Thus its exact integer set is P'=W union {p_2}. All nine W
points remain exposed by their fixed normals. The only nonvertex
integer point is the center p_2 of the y=0 diamond. The old height
function remains Jensen-affine under restriction and removes exactly
this center when its height is required to be integral.

For the five-point diamond D, three noncollinear corners give a
critical three-set witness. A four-corner witness is impossible
because every deletion triangle contains the center. Any four-point
subset including the center also contains an opposite corner pair,
so its center is not a vertex; such a set cannot be a critical
witness. The five-point set likewise fails convex position. Hence
h(D)=3. The finite-source union inequality gives h(P')<=3+5=8.

For the eight-point lower witness V=W minus {p_3}, each own point
is excluded from its deletion hull by its exposing normal. The
omitted p_3 is outside conv(V), because its y=0 height z=2 exceeds
that of every remaining point on that supporting face. The other
omitted source point p_2 is outside the deletion hull removing
p_0: its intersection with y=0 lies in the segment [p_1,p_6],
where x-z=1, whereas x-z=0 at p_2. Thus the full deletion kernel
contains no P' point. Every proper subfamily contains its omitted
witness. This proves h(P')=8 exactly. The integral graph consists
of nine vertices with no other integer point in their hull, so
its deletion family gives h(T')=9 exactly.

## 2. Full body and both actual measures

The graph hull conv(W_hat) has affine dimension four. Its product
with the full s-simplex K is therefore a full body in R^(4+s).
Jensen affinity forces each actual coarse integer fiber to be
{g(p)} times K. Conversely every such graph point is in the hull,
including the fractional p_2 midpoint, so every fiber asserted by
the source is present and exact.

Consequently the fine measure has exactly nine positive equal K
fibers and total intrinsic H_s mass 9V_K. The coarse measure has
exactly ten positive equal K fibers and total mass 10V_K. There
are no zero-mass outlier fibers in this strengthened body. Every
product generating fiber is fine-sampled, proving C=conv(S_fine).
All full (s+1)-dimensional coarse volumes are zero, but neither
intrinsic measure is zero. This distinction is kept throughout.

## 3. Exact fine maximum

The ordinary centroid of an own K fiber gives unnormalized mass
at least Gamma_s V_K in every containing ambient closed cap.
The fixed normal gap of one and tilt two isolate the canonical
simplex caps from every other positive fine fiber: their margins
there are at most 1-1/(s+1)-2<0. The 9(s+1) caps cover the full
fine source and each has exactly Gamma_s V_K mass. Thus its
global maximal depth is exactly Gamma_s/9, including all boundary
centers and all possible oblique halfspaces.

## 4. Coarse lower bound: all normals

At a_2=(p_2,1/2,c_K), a containing cap can be moved inward until
its boundary passes through a_2. This can only decrease its mass.
If its continuous x-normal is nonzero, the two displayed pairs
of graph bases are opposite about the graph of p_2. Their own
centroid thresholds are therefore t,-t for each pair, with no
assumption on the other ambient normal coefficients. The proved
paired-tail inequality contributes at least 2 Gamma_s V_K from
each pair. The own fiber supplies another Gamma_s V_K. Thus every
such cap has mass at least 5 Gamma_s V_K.

If the x-normal is zero, the cap contains the entire own K and
at least one full fiber in each opposite pair. Closed boundaries
can only add fibers. Its mass is at least 3V_K, which exceeds
5 Gamma_s V_K because Gamma_s<=1/2. The whole-space restriction
case is harmless as well. Therefore the normalized coarse depth
at a_2 is at least Gamma_s/2 for EVERY cap orientation.

## 5. Coarse upper bound: every possible center

The caps lambda_r(x)-1/(s+1)-2y>=0 isolate the y=0 face, since
every other coarse integer base has y>=1. Each has the canonical
simplex cap on all five face fibers, hence exact mass
5 Gamma_s V_K. They cover the entire p_2 fiber.

At any other coarse base p_i in W, at least one of the two
disjoint opposite pairs omits p_i. Averaging its two exposure
inequalities proves that the normal's old unit gap also holds
against p_2. Thus the original tilt-two simplex caps isolate that
fiber from ALL other coarse fibers, including the newly admitted
center. They cover the whole own fiber with cap mass Gamma_s V_K.
All centers have now been covered: the p_2 fiber has upper depth
Gamma_s/2, and each of the other nine fibers has upper depth
Gamma_s/10. Combining with the previous section proves the global
coarse maximum Gamma_s/2 and exact fine/coarse ratio 2/9.

The strict comparison Gamma_s/9<Gamma_(s+1)/8 for s>=2 follows
from the earlier audited all-real convexity of log Gamma. Fine
integer rank remains four, with OC target Gamma_s/16. Dropping
one integer restriction changes the measure and admits a new
center. Neither the fine OC target nor a claim about the different
coarse source is contradicted.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
